version_boundary.rule: Use this snapshot to explain control-flow shape only. Official documentation and observed 2.1.209 behavior override version-sensitive details.

mechanisms.name: iterative_query_state_machine
mechanisms.evidence: QueryParams separate immutable inputs from mutable cross-iteration State; queryLoop runs while(true) and carries transition, turn count, compaction and stop-hook state.

mechanisms.name: model_request_assembly
mechanisms.evidence: Each model request combines meta user context, system prefix, thinking config, tools, permissions, active agents, MCP state, query tracking, effort and task budget.

mechanisms.name: streaming_fallback_tombstones
mechanisms.evidence: Partial assistant messages, especially signed thinking blocks, are tombstoned on fallback and the streaming tool executor is recreated.

mechanisms.name: content_block_event_fragmentation
mechanisms.evidence: Each content_block_stop can yield a separate AssistantMessage, while final usage and stop_reason are completed later from message_delta. One API response can therefore occupy multiple JSONL assistant records.

mechanisms.name: streaming_tool_execution
mechanisms.evidence: tool_use blocks are detected as they stream; the executor may start tools and yield completed results before the model stream has fully ended.

mechanisms.name: non_streaming_concurrency_partitioning
mechanisms.evidence: In the fallback/non-streaming runTools path, only consecutive concurrency-safe tool calls are batched, with a default maximum of 10; non-safe calls run serially and context modifiers are applied in original tool order.

mechanisms.name: streaming_safe_unsafe_barriers
mechanisms.evidence: The primary streaming path starts safe tools while blocks arrive and uses unsafe-tool barriers to preserve ordering. The inspected evidence does not establish that this path shares the runTools default concurrency limit of 10.

mechanisms.name: tool_validation_feedback
mechanisms.evidence: Schema and semantic validation failures are returned as error tool_result messages with the original tool_use_id instead of escaping the agent loop.

mechanisms.name: pretool_permission_pipeline
mechanisms.evidence: Bash classification may start speculatively; PreToolUse hooks can alter input, add context or stop; hook decisions then pass through settings/rule-based deny and ask checks before execution, so hook allow does not bypass explicit permission policy.

mechanisms.name: bash_sandbox_execution
mechanisms.evidence: Permission and sandbox are separate controls: permission authorizes a Bash action, while sandbox selection and shell adapters constrain its actual filesystem, network and process capabilities.

mechanisms.name: context_authority_layers
mechanisms.evidence: Git state is a conversation-start system-context snapshot, while CLAUDE.md and current date enter as meta user context; system and user context use different message roles and cache behavior.

mechanisms.name: post_tool_attachment_queue
mechanisms.evidence: Queued commands, task notifications, skill discovery and memory attachments are injected after the tool batch so tool_use and tool_result adjacency is preserved; queues are scoped differently for main and subagent contexts.

mechanisms.name: compaction_control_system
mechanisms.evidence: Compaction reserves output headroom, has recursion guards, composes with other context systems, and trips a circuit breaker after three consecutive failures.

mechanisms.name: append_log_and_message_dag
mechanisms.evidence: Persistence can be suppressed, files materialize on first user/assistant message, parentUuid and logicalParentUuid form the chain, parallel tool-use siblings are repaired during loading, and loadFullLog rebuilds from the newest leaf.

mechanisms.name: checkpoint_and_resume_recovery
mechanisms.evidence: File-history snapshots are associated with user prompts; resume reconstructs conversation/file history, repairs interrupted tool-use state and emits resume lifecycle context. Checkpoint recovery is distinct from session fork and cannot undo arbitrary external side effects.

mechanisms.name: subagent_context_isolation
mechanisms.evidence: Normal subagents start from delegated prompt plus agent context; fork paths may inherit filtered parent messages and exact tool/prompt prefixes; permission, abort and app-state sharing differ for sync and async agents.

mechanisms.name: fork_vs_normal_agent_path
mechanisms.evidence: Fork children can reuse the parent's exact system/tool prefix for cache identity, while normal agents build their own prompt and tool pool; async agents receive independent lifecycle management.
